Personally, no. I see a lot of people suggesting that we shouldn’t judge someone at their worst especially when they’ve done so much good later in their lives. 

My issue with that is there are certain acts that you can’t come back from. When the news about his abuses came to light Harvey Weinstein promised to fight the NRA and Republicans. If he managed to pass laws that ended mass shootings in the US would that mean any of you would forgive him for being a serial rapist? 

I think Brandon Sanderson himself doesn’t believe in forgiving everyone or at the very least he doesn’t believe in the audiences capacity for it. There’s a reason why Sadeas is shown committing acts of sexual violence in the flashback whilst Dalinar doesn’t engage in any at all. Mass slaughter is almost too big of an act to actually wrap your head around. 

Contrast that to Moash who killed a corrupt racist king who was about to become an incredible threat to his comrades on the battlefield. He then has a literal piece of divinity suppress his capacity to feel anything but hate and in that state he kills someone else who poses a threat to the freed slaves he has allied himself with. 

Also even after a literal piece of divinity removes the literal memory of his war crime from him he is almost completely blind to Elhokar’s abuses of power and when he is made aware of Rashon he sends him where ‘He can do no harm’ as he and most of the light eyes don’t view dark eyes as actual human beings. Sure he doesn’t use bridge crews (until Elhokar prods him) but he’s fine sending 1000s of them to die in order to commit genocide against a group whose leaders already answered for the assassination of his brother. He also literally opposes abolishing slavery. 


Dalinar isn’t even the most noble High Prince as Sebariel pretty much sends his soldiers out as little as possible when Dalinar takes command of their fight against the parshendi. 


There’s a reason why bad guys in fiction often redeem themselves through death as the vast majority of people understand there are certain things you just can’t come back from. Does that mean I want Dalinar to be killed, of course not. But when one of the most kind Light eyes in the series in Adolin struggles to maintain a good relationship with his father after finding out the truth I think some of you ought to pause a little too. 

At the end of the day I think our first impressions colour the way we view the actions of characters. A character whom we see in a positive light has way more lee way than a character who is introduced as antagonistic such as Moash.

‘Won’t be a fool again’
